newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts see higher Q1 97 earnings at Viag.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see higher Q1 97 earnings at Viag.

text.p: Group profits at German diversified utility Viag AG for 1996 are expected to fall because of a less favourable tax environment for the group, but analysts say fundamentals at Viag are sound.
Viag will announce final details of its 1996 figures and first quarter 1997 figures at its annual news conference in Munich on Friday.
The outlook for 1997 is generally positive, with most commentators forecasting strong growth for the first quarter.

Peter Antes, utilities analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank, forecast a 9.3 percent rise in first quarter pre-tax profits to 730 million marks, and he expects first quarter sales to rise 5.9 percent to 11.5 billion marks.

"I expect them to say that operating profits rose in the first quarter -- any other details on operating profits is unlikely," said Antes, who is maintaining his market neutral recommendation for the stock.
Robert Willis, German equities analyst at Schroder Securities in London, said that 1995 headline earnings were inflated as Viag by crucial tax advantages
These accrued by offsetting losses in part of its electricity business against 700 million mark gains from the disposal of PWA.
This meant the headline figures looked better than the real underlying story.
"This means the profit figures will look lower on the 1996 headline figures, but the fundamentals looked better last year," said Willis.
The big driver for earnings growth at Viag will be its traditional energy division, led by its highly-profitable Bayernwerk unit.
Willis sees earnings per share (EPS) by the DVFA German analysts' method at 34.3 marks in 1996. He forecasts a rise in EPS to 37.2 marks in 1997 and 45.5 marks in 1998.
Antes is forecasting a 13.3 percent fall in 1996 group profit net of minorities to 1.145 billion marks, because of higher tax charges.

His forecast for the 1996 DVFA result net of minorites is for a fall of three percent to 961 million marks, while his DVFA EPS outlook for 1996 is 36 marks, down 22.3 percent, which is around the market consensus.
Antes 1997 EPS outlook 39 marks per share, below the general market consensus outlook of 39.50 marks .
